summary: Streamers are leaving or considering leaving Kick after Ice Poseidon (Paul Denino) streamed a encounter with a sex worker without disclosing that others were hiding nearby, while Kick CEO Eddie Craven posted laughing emotes in chat. Kick's response was seen as weak, and it only removed Denino from its front page and featured category. Some creators quit on principle, while others like Kelly (MrsViolence) and Bree say they can't afford to leave, citing Kick's better pay compared with Twitch's reduced revenue splits and the harassment they faced on Twitch.
one_line: Streamers weigh leaving Kick after its CEO laughed at Ice Poseidon's sex worker 'prank' stream, though many depend on its better pay.
key_facts: Paul Denino, known as Ice Poseidon, streamed the encounter on September 21 from Brisbane, Australia, with fellow streamer Sam Pepper hiding in an adjacent bedroom.

A man named Andy paid the sex worker $500 and asked for her consent to film; she tried to leave after a text about the people in the other room, but Andy stopped her, and she called the encounter 'creepy.'
Kick CEO Eddie Craven posted laughing emotes in the stream chat during the incident.
Denino disputed claims of a 'hidden camera' and alleged the interaction was legal, saying the sex worker approved filming for an extra fee.

Kick lured Twitch streamers with non-exclusive streaming deals, light moderation and a 95/5 revenue split; its first year has been marked by controversy, including ties to a crypto gambling site also owned by Craven.
Kick removed Denino from the front page and featured category but did not ban him; Bree called this a 'start' and said contracts likely complicate a ban.
Kick's public post said community and public safety 'cannot be compromised,' and the company told 404 Media it 'continuously review[s] and refine[s]' policies; it did not respond to TechCrunch.
Rachel (TheFoodieWaifu) and Bob (BobDuckNWeave) decided to leave Kick, with Bob saying Craven laughing was 'more than enough to stamp out any hope' of policy improvement.
Twitch's default sub split for Partners is 50/50; it ended a premium 70/30 deal last year, and its new Partner Plus program has steep requirements that exclude most Partners.
Kelly (MrsViolence) earned a little over $1,000 per month on Twitch with over 700 subscribers, which fell to about $400 after the changes and now around $120.
Kelly says she makes over $1,000 per month on Kick with only 145 subscribers, covering rent and groceries, and refuses to return to Twitch.
Bree said she cannot return to Twitch because of harassment and threats against her life there, and that streaming is her livelihood.
